parallel.requirements: The parent recognized exact C++ behavior, std-only Rust, Cargo/rustc buildability, CLI parsing, and black-box reference probing; it also expanded the task into a detailed inferred immer/stoi spec.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent chose a workflow with Recon, Build, Judge, Assemble, Verify, and Fix phases, but active work during the run remained parent probing plus three Recon child agents and one retry.
parallel.implementation: No Rust implementation was completed or captured. The planned candidate build phase sat after the recon await and was never reached before the run ended.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No assembly into /output completed; artifact validation found no files and final.txt was empty.
parallel.verification: The parent and recon children did extensive reference-binary and oracle checks, but these only verified the inferred behavior and not a final Rust artifact.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The process timed out with the workflow killed, recon children in progress/interrupted, no delivered source tree, and official evaluation 0/40.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same exact-output, CLI, std-only, and black-box requirements, including UB-like negative values, stoi abort behavior, and INT_MAX loop behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One actor kept ownership of investigation, implementation, repair, verification, and delivery without delegation or handoff.
serial.implementation: It wrote a Rust port with test14.rs, CLI parsing, immer module files for trie/vector/transient/raw slots, and Cargo.toml, then fixed compile errors and warnings.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The implementation was integrated directly in /output; artifact validation captured test14.rs, module files, Cargo files, and rustc/cargo release binaries.
serial.verification: It ran small, negative, boundary, deep-trie, stoi, debug-build, cargo-build, byte-exact, and INT_MAX checks before finalizing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator accepted the artifact 40/40; remaining prompt-style deviations, such as module placement outside src, did not prevent the official pass.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel understood the prompt and inferred a rich immer/stoi behavioral spec, including leaf size, wrapping arithmetic, and out-of-range behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same obligations and specifically locked down negative inputs, stoi errors, no-arg defaults, and INT_MAX behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement understanding was broadly comparable, but serial converted the requirements into a deliverable while parallel kept expanding the pre-implementation spec.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated to a workflow whose first executable phase was three recon agents; build, judge, assemble, verify, and fix ownership came only after recon completed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial retained one-owner control and moved from probing to writing module files directly in /output.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's decomposition separated all investigation from implementation and made implementation a later dependency; serial used a linear but integrated ownership path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were detailed but scoped to recon; one stalled stoi retry restarted from the same broad brief rather than a checkpointed handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept discoveries in the same parent context and applied them to the implementation without cross-agent transfer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced cross-actor context boundaries before any implementation; serial avoided transfer loss by maintaining one local context.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel never reached candidate implementation; no /tmp/candA or /tmp/candB tree was visible during polling and no /output artifact was captured.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote trie, vector, transient, raw slot, CLI, entry, and Cargo files, then fixed compiler errors.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The decisive implementation difference is absence versus presence of a Rust project, not a smaller algorithmic mismatch in delivered code.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel workflow children were started, one was retried after a stall, and the workflow state ended killed with result null.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed local work, consumed its own verification results, and produced a final answer describing the delivered artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did not retrieve or promote child results into build work before timeout; serial kept results in-process through finalization.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel did not assemble a final tree in /output; artifact validation saw an empty directory and no expected entry file.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated all source files and binaries into /output, and artifact validation listed them.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no parallel merge collision; the material difference is that serial assembled deliverables while parallel never reached assembly.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified only reference behavior and golden corpora while no Rust artifact existed; official evaluation later passed 0/40.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified the Rust binary against C++ on small, negative, boundary, deep, stoi, debug, and INT_MAX cases before official 40/40 success.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's checks were pre-implementation evidence; serial's checks exercised the actual deliverable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full 2399 second budget, timed out, and ended with process_ok false.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed in about 1291 agent seconds, did not time out, and left official retry/budget unused.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's closure was a hard timeout before delivery, while serial closed normally after verification.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This is a serial-only pass: the serial run delivered and verified a Rust project that the official evaluator accepted 40/40, while the parallel run timed out before any implementation or assembled artifact reached /output and therefore scored 0/40. The evidenced process difference is not that the parallel code had a subtle implementation defect; it had no submitted implementation. Parallel deferred build/assembly behind a recon-only workflow phase and also restarted a stalled stoi recon child without a checkpoint, consuming the available budget before productive implementation began.
parallel_contributors: Workflow implementation was gated behind a Recon await, and the run was killed while recon children were still active.
The stalled stoi retry restarted broad setup/probing without inherited checkpoint state.
serial_contributors: The single actor moved from probing to writing /output files and fixed build errors directly.
Serial verified the actual Rust deliverable, including the INT_MAX case, before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No delivered parallel implementation exists to compare algorithmically; the decisive difference is delivery lifecycle, not a normal coding bug.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
